sections.h2: Who to call about a Pender bill or a value
sections.html:
Both property tax offices are at 803 S. Walker Street in Burgaw. Tax Administration keeps the appraisal and listing records. Tax Collections sends the bills and takes the money. Questions about listing, billing and assessed values go to the assessment side, not to collections.

  • Value or record questions: the assessment line, (910) 259-1221.
  • Payments and balances: Tax Collections, (910) 259-1222, or P.O. Box 1047, Burgaw, NC 28425 by mail.
  • Office hours: weekdays from eight in the morning until five.

One wrinkle in Pender: some towns bill separately. Collections handles the county levy plus Burgaw, Watha, St. Helena and Atkinson. Surf City and Topsail Beach run their own billing, and their real and personal property taxes also fall due September 1. A coastal house can carry both a county bill and a town bill.

Every real property parcel was repriced to its market value as of January 1, 2026. The previous effective date was January 1, 2019, so seven years went by between the two.

In 2023 the commissioners passed a resolution moving Pender to a four-year cycle, so the county plans to revalue again every four years after 2026. State law alone only demands an eighth-year reappraisal under G.S. 105-286. Ask Tax Administration for the next scheduled date.

A few dates from this cycle still matter:

  • Owners have until December 31, 2026 to appeal.
  • A revaluation sets worth, not the bill. Rates come later, set by the commissioners and town boards, normally by July.

Any tax figure quoted before then is a guess.

sections.h2: How to contest a Pender value
sections.html:
File the 2026 Tax Appeal Form. You can complete it online, or print it and send it to Pender County Tax Department, P.O. Box 67, Burgaw, NC 28425. Walking it into the Walker Street counter also works.

The county suggests three steps. Start by reading the property record card on the public access site for errors in square footage, features or condition. Next, run the county's sales comparison tool against your value. If the record is accurate and the number still seems too high, request a hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review and wait for the written decision.

An appeal has to be about value. A big jump or a feared tax increase is not a ground. Strong files usually include:

  • comparable sales dated before January 1, 2026
  • photographs or plans showing condition and upgrades
  • a recent fee appraisal from a purchase or refinance, if you have one

If you lose, the state Property Tax Commission is the next stop. Written notice is due a month after the county board mails its ruling (G.S. 105-290).

Bills are mailed in late August and the tax comes due September 1. You owe no extra charge until after January 5.

Pender property tax dates
WhenWhat happens
January 1 to 31Personal property listing
Late AugustBills mailed, before September 1
September 1Real estate and personal property due
January 5Final day before interest, penalties and legal remedies
January 6Interest begins: 2% for January, then 3/4 of 1% monthly
First Wednesday in MarchUnpaid real estate taxes listed as delinquent

Vehicles on the registration cycle follow other dates. The statewide interest rule is G.S. 105-360.

Payment options are eCheck online, phone, the counter, or the box outside the building. For mail, only a Postal Service postmark sets the date, and a business meter stamp will not. Early payers can write "prepayment" plus the parcel number on a check before the bill arrives. Installment schedules are possible while no legal action is pending.

The state offers three tax relief programs on a primary residence, and one owner can use only one. In Pender you apply to the county assessor on Form AV-9. The form tells counties to take applications up to June 1.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or half the home's value comes off the taxable amount. Income must stay under $38,800 for 2026 (NCDOR form).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 is removed for a qualifying owner. No age or income test applies.
  • Circuit breaker: your bill is capped at 4% of income (5% if income runs up to 150% of the ceiling) and the remainder is deferred.

Full rules sit in G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1C. A deferral is recorded as a lien and is repaid when the house sells. Before listing, ask the assessor whether yours carries one.

sections.h2: If a Pender payment bounces or runs late
sections.html:
A returned check or failed online payment adds a fee of 10% or $25, whichever is greater (G.S. 105-357(b)(2)), plus any interest and penalty. The county voids the receipt and wants cash, a money order or certified funds to fix it.

Collections uses the full range of remedies the general statutes allow. Its combined collection rate was 97.23% for the year closed June 30, 2025, so nearly every bill gets paid and the office follows up on the rest.

  • Delinquent real estate taxes are listed on the first Wednesday of March.
  • The last interest-free day is January 5, so a payment dated January 6 already carries the 2% charge.
  • Dates can change, so confirm with the office.

Unpaid tax can end in a foreclosure sale at the courthouse door, and G.S. 105-374 lets the owner redeem before confirmation. Contact the office long before that point.

The year's lien rides with the land (G.S. 105-355), so your closing attorney orders a payoff and takes it from your proceeds.

  • Find out whether a town bills the parcel in addition to the county.
  • Look for a delinquent balance on the March list.
  • Verify that monthly prepayments reached the right account.
  • Ask about any deferral lien from a relief program.

If you sell ahead of the September 1 due date, you and the buyer still need to agree on who covers that year. Owners who are behind and in a hurry can request cash offers, then compare each against the net after the payoff the collector quotes. A cash sale skips the lender's timeline, though the tax payoff still comes out at closing.

sections.h2: Steps before you list a Pender house
sections.html:
A short round of calls up front keeps tax surprises off the closing table. Work through the list in order and hand the answers to your closing attorney.

  1. Call the assessment line, (910) 259-1221, and ask what value sits on the record and whether the 2026 repricing changed it.
  2. Pull the property record card online and compare square footage, features and condition with the house as it stands today.
  3. Call Tax Collections, (910) 259-1222, for the balance on each parcel and ask whether any prepayment was posted.
  4. Ask whether Surf City or Topsail Beach, or any other town, bills the parcel separately.
  5. Ask whether an exclusion or circuit breaker deferral is attached, since a sale can end it.

Bring the parcel number and your latest bill to any counter visit. Staff can then pull the account in a minute instead of searching by name.

faqs.q: Where is the Pender County tax office?
faqs.a: 803 S. Walker Street in Burgaw. The office keeps weekday hours and an outside drop box for payments after closing time.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 appeal window still open?
faqs.a: Owners have until December 31, 2026 to appeal. Confirm the status with the tax department at (910) 259-1221.

faqs.q: Which Pender towns send their own tax bills?
faqs.a: Surf City and Topsail Beach bill and collect their own real and personal taxes. The county collector handles the county plus Burgaw, Watha, St. Helena and Atkinson.
Under the 2023 resolution, the cycle is every four years from the 2026 date. Ask the tax office to confirm the next effective date.

faqs.q: Does Pender allow installment payments of tax?
faqs.a: Yes, while no legal action is open on the account. Call before the bill turns delinquent, since the window shrinks afterward.
